items.title: Choice Paid $24 Million to Walk Away From Buying Spain’s Sercotel
items.summary: Choice earns a cut of its franchisees’ room sales. Buying Sercotel would have left it owing rent even when bookings slowed.

items.title: The Unproven Economics of the Weekend Cruise
items.summary: Cruise lines are putting some of their biggest ships on shorter trips, but the financial evidence that those voyages generate better returns remains thin.

items.title: Why Scaling AI Agents Is Harder Than Building Them
items.summary: Scaling AI agents is less about the model than the systems, talent, and infrastructure around it. As travel companies move from pilots into production, they must decide which capabilities differentiate the business and which are better handled by a specialist.

items.title: Regional Visitors Keep Oman’s Arrivals Steady but Can’t Fill Its Hotels
items.summary: Oman’s arrivals have held up this year, but its hotels lost more than a tenth of their guests and revenue as Europeans stayed away. Regional travelers are still arriving but make shorter visits at lower rates.

items.title: Air India CEO Wants More Widebodies as International Ambitions Grow
items.summary: Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam thinks the carrier has been "punching below its weight." He is now planning for the airline he wants it to become, not the one it is today.

items.title: Thailand’s 2032 Tourism Plan Chases Spending, Not Arrivals
items.summary: Thailand’s $118 billion goal targets spending rather than arrivals, which have stalled at about 33 million. Rising prices will surely lift revenue regardless, but higher rates aren’t the same as higher value, and the plan has no budget yet for the terminals, marinas and guides ne

items.title: Booking.com Bets Travelers Will Research With AI but Book With It
items.summary: AI may own the start of the trip, but Booking.com is betting trust and payments decide who gets the booking. Its experience with superapps, where daily use never became travel spending, suggests generative chatbots may face the same problem.

items.title: Booking Takes $1 Billion Hit Over Possible FTC Settlement, Sees ‘Mixed’ Travel Market
items.summary: The Middle East conflict and higher airfares continue to make their mark industrywide.
